problem_statement: John Doe 3D Portfolio currently renders Home, About, Work, Contact navigation, a dark violet hero with a 3D desktop computer canvas, service cards, a vertical Work Experience timeline, rotating technology icons, Carrent/JobIT/Trip Guide project cards, Testimonials, and an Earth contact form. Turn this starter into a coherent Spatial Product Engineer portfolio that demonstrates the ability to build polished 3D product websites from the existing assets, not a renamed template. The site should introduce a real design-engineering identity in the hero, make the 3D computer and Earth canvases feel connected to product prototyping and global collaboration, convert the service cards into clear specialties, replace the repeated Starbucks/Tesla/Shopify/Meta timeline with a credible studio/product-build narrative, and reshape the project/testimonial/contact copy so Carrent, JobIT, and Trip Guide read as case-study evidence with role, outcome, stack, and interaction context. Keep the one-page route, existing nav anchors, dark purple/black visual language, local project screenshots, technology icon balls, 3D computer, Earth scene, star field, form behavior, and responsive layout. Repair the long empty visual rhythm between sections so desktop and mobile visitors encounter meaningful content at each scroll position rather than a starter portfolio with generic names and repeated bullets.
required_content: Hero title and document title present a coherent Spatial Product Engineer or 3D Product Engineer identity instead of John Doe.
About/service cards explain 3D UI, spatial interaction, product prototyping, and front-end systems using the existing card/icon language.
Experience timeline replaces default company names and repeated bullets with a credible product/studio build history and varied outcomes.
Projects section uses Carrent, JobIT, and Trip Guide screenshots as case-study evidence with visible Role, Outcome, Stack, and interaction/design context.
Testimonials and contact copy support the same design-engineering portfolio narrative and keep the Earth/star canvas area purposeful.
Desktop and mobile scroll states remove long empty gaps while preserving the dark 3D portfolio atmosphere.
A shared 'Spatial delivery cadence' strip names the Prototype, Systemize, and Ship build phases and appears in BOTH the About specialties context and the Projects case-study context.
Selecting a phase updates a live readout of the active phase and the recommended next step (real client-side interaction, no page reload).
The phase-step strip wraps cleanly and never overflows horizontally on tablet or mobile while matching the dark violet rounded-card chrome.
design_constraints: Preserve the existing dark violet/black palette, gradient text, rounded cards, vertical timeline, animated cards, technology icon balls, and Three.js canvas emphasis.
Do not replace the site with a flat resume, SaaS landing page, or unrelated marketing layout; the result should still feel like a polished interactive 3D portfolio.
Use the existing screenshots and icons intentionally; project images must remain legible and connected to the written case-study content.
Keep section spacing cinematic but controlled: no large blank corridors between hero, about, timeline, tech, projects, testimonials, and contact.
Mobile should stack cards, timeline, projects, testimonials, and contact form cleanly with no text overlap or horizontal overflow.
The spatial delivery cadence must be one shared component reused across the About and Projects sections (consistent delivery story), not a one-off block in a single section.
The phase readout must reflect the currently selected phase live; a static or stale readout that ignores the click is incorrect.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial preserve the hero, nav, 3D computer, and dark background treatment.
desktop_about / tablet_about / mobile_about show the specialties and the spatial delivery cadence strip.
desktop_cadence_systemize and desktop_cadence_ship show the live readout updated to the selected phase.
desktop_projects and desktop_work show the shared cadence echoed into the Projects/experience context.
mobile_cadence and tablet_cadence keep the phase strip wrapped with no horizontal overflow.

change_completion: Default John Doe starter identity, default companies, repeated timeline bullets, and generic project intro are replaced by one coherent spatial/product-engineering narrative.
Hero, About, Work Experience, Tech, Projects, Testimonials, and Contact all contribute to the same portfolio story.
Project cards expose visible case-study evidence, roles, outcomes, stack, and interaction/product context while retaining Carrent, JobIT, and Trip Guide images.
3D computer, Earth, star field, and tech balls remain purposeful visual anchors rather than decorative leftovers.
design_consistency: Dark violet 3D portfolio style, gradient accents, card/timeline styling, and cinematic canvas treatment are preserved.
New content uses short scannable labels and does not overcrowd cards or timeline nodes.
The page rhythm is tightened without losing the immersive atmosphere.
regression: Home/About/Work/Contact anchors, contact form, project images, tech icons, and 3D canvases still render.
No local assets or sections are deleted to simplify the transformation.
responsive: Mobile hero/about/projects states show meaningful content without horizontal overflow, clipped text, or large empty stretches.
Project and testimonial cards remain readable at narrow widths.

author_notes: Repo-grounded task on the ladunjexa/reactjs18-3d-portfolio React 18 + Vite + Three.js 3D portfolio (threejs-3d-portfolio project). The starter renders a dark-violet hero with a 3D desktop-computer canvas, About service cards, a vertical Work Experience timeline, rotating technology icon balls, Carrent/JobIT/Trip Guide project screenshots, Testimonials, and an Earth contact scene. This L4 task adds a shared interactive 'Spatial delivery cadence' strip reused across the About and Projects sections, exercising design continuity, cross-section structure, a live phase-selection interaction, deterministic visual fidelity of the phase tiles, and mobile responsive layout. It tests complete design-engineering ability across canvas-heavy states and narrow viewports on real built-and-served DOM, not just source reading.
